_legend.array_order: Within each section, earlier = higher trust/relevance in the only sense we can back (trace tier, then within-type score). There is NO comparable score across sections.
_legend.grounded_facts: Derived facts whose evidence chain is traceable (a linked verbatim quote + session). Each carries evidence[] (the ground-truth quote) and corroborated_by (raw_context units that independently say the same thing).
_legend.how_to_use: Answer from grounded_facts + their evidence quotes when the chain is solid; consult topic_rollups for coverage/counting; open raw_context to verify or when facts are missing; re-verify anything in needs_verification. Never treat a derived fact as truth over the raw evidence.
_legend.ids: Every unit has a stable id. Cross-references (corroborated_by / shared_evidence_with / aggregates / possible_support) use these ids so you can trace any chain.
_legend.needs_verification: Derived assertions with a broken/absent evidence chain. DO NOT trust as-is. Follow possible_support into raw_context and re-reason before using.
_legend.raw_context: Verbatim original conversation windows/turns, extraction-agnostic. THIS IS GROUND TRUTH. When a derived fact is thin or a needs_verification item is unproven, read here and reason directly. Grouped by session, ordered by turn.
_legend.read_as: recall organized by EVIDENCE-CHAIN TRUST — NOT by whether your question is answered
_legend.topic_rollups: Write-time aggregates over many memories. Use for 'which / how many / list all' breadth questions. Prose digest — may embed importance numbers; not a quotable fact. aggregates shows which grounded_facts it rolls up; backing_present=false means it asserts more than the facts returned here.
_legend.trust_model: grounded_facts and topic_rollups are DERIVED by an extraction model (the memory write path). They can be generalized, incomplete, or WRONG — they are NOT ground truth. The ONLY authoritative content is the verbatim raw_context and the evidence quotes. If a derived fact looks thin, ambiguous, or conflicts, DO NOT trust it as truth — re-reason from raw_context and cite the raw quote instead.
